service:

=== V3 ===
-- Projects: a piece of work the owner does for a client. Each project belongs to one client
-- (client_id -> clients.id), so the projects list can show the client's name via the join.
CREATE TABLE projects (
    id        BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    name      VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    client_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(id)
);
=== V25 ===
-- Two clients cannot share an email. Enforce uniqueness at the DB level too (the last line of
-- defence), matching the duplicate check in the server (ClientsPostLogic) and the error the front-end
-- surfaces. Applies to every client row regardless of archived state: an email already on file — even
-- an archived one — cannot be reused for a new client.
ALTER TABLE clients
    ADD CONSTRAINT clients_email_unique UNIQUE (email);

-- Each project (job) carries a short reference code, set when the job is created. The code is
-- unique across projects so no two jobs share one — enforce that at the DB level (the last line of
-- defence), matching the duplicate check in the server (ProjectsPostLogic) and the error the
-- front-end surfaces. Nullable: projects predating this column have no code (multiple NULLs are
-- allowed under a UNIQUE constraint), so the uniqueness only binds the codes actually set.

    ADD COLUMN code VARCHAR(255);

    ADD CONSTRAINT projects_code_unique UNIQUE (code);

- `projects.ts` types/mutation carry `code`.
